newsitem.title: GERMANY: Official says EU plans postal subsidies crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Official says EU plans postal subsidies crackdown.

text.p: The European Commission plans to crack down on post office subsidies and state aid in competitive areas of the European mail and parcels market, a senior official said on Thursday.
Jean-Francois Pons, deputy director general of DG IV, the competition directorate, said the Commission would publish a notice on competition rules for the postal sector within the next few weeks.
The notice would take account of criticism (by private competitors) of state support for national post administrations, he said in a speech at the eighth World Express & Mail conference here.
The Commission would seek to avoid cross-subsidies and state aid but did not want to see post offices abandoning their commitment to public services, he added, without giving further details.
"We are drafting the last version of the notice, taking account of the criticisms which have been received. I hope the notice will be submitted in a few weeks," he said.
"The notice is not a directive through the back-door. It defines rules in competitive areas (of the post market)," he told the audience of express and mail operators and post office managers.
EU ministers agreed last December to de-regulate the market for letters above 350g or packages costing more than five times the standard letter price from 1998.
This prompted criticism by postal users groups and companies such as UPS and FedEx that full liberalisation was being delayed until 2003.
But Pons said: "It is a liberalisation of three percent of all post. It is a small step in the liberalisation (process)."
The Commission, he added, had been surprised by the division between member states over postal liberalisation, with some states worried about post office job losses and threats to rural services.
